project.name: Mongoose
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged checkout `e5b0528aca2524d15bf421ce36c64afa8db137c8`, which is an ancestor of both metadata commits. That staged source still contains the fully unchecked `memcpy(..., pkt->pay.len)` in `rx_icmp`; metadata commit `a88a11c2` is already a partial fix that introduces `left` for the copy but still computes the checksum over the uncapped length. All anchors below use the staged checkout's exact line map.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 compiled and reproduced the crash from this staged ancestor checkout. The local `patch.diff` reflects the later metadata fix line map, so Stage 02 anchors the trace to this reproduced snapshot instead of to the patch context.

classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports a dynamic stack overflow because `ifp->tx.buf` points into the fuzz target's VLA-backed stack object `t`, but the underlying bug is an unchecked out-of-bounds write of attacker-controlled ICMP payload bytes into a fixed 1540-byte transmit buffer.

bug_description.original: An overflow occurs in the rx_icmp function.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 131033` in `rx_icmp` on the staged Mongoose checkout `e5b0528aca2524d15bf421ce36c64afa8db137c8`, an ancestor of the metadata commits `a88a11c2` and `9680b8cc`. In the fuzz target, `pktlen` is fixed to 1540 and stack object `t` backs the entire `mip_if`, including a 1540-byte transmit buffer that `if_init` exposes as `ifp->tx`. `mip_rx` then aliases the exact 131071-byte witness into `pkt.raw`, accepts it as an IPv4 frame because the destination MAC is `00:00:00:00:00:00` like the zeroed interface MAC, and forwards it to the ICMP path. On that path, `mkpay(pkt, pkt->icmp + 1)` derives `pkt->pay.len = 131033` from the remaining input bytes after fixed Ethernet/IP/ICMP headers; the vulnerable receive logic ignores the witness IPv4 IHL byte `0x49` and total-length field `0x0003`, so the full trailing span is treated as payload. `rx_icmp` only checks `pkt->icmp->type == 8` and `pkt->ip->dst == ifp->ip`; with zeroed `cfg`, `ifp->ip == 0`, so witness destination `0.0.0.0` passes. The staged vulnerable source then executes `memcpy(icmp + 1, pkt->pay.buf, pkt->pay.len)` with no transmit-buffer length check. Because `icmp + 1` is 38 bytes into a 1540-byte TX buffer, only 1502 payload bytes fit, but the call copies all 131033 bytes into the VLA-backed stack object, producing the saved overflow. Metadata commit `a88a11c2` only partially fixes this path by capping the copy length; `9680b8cc` completes the fix by also using the capped length for `ipcsum`.

source.description: First project-code consumption on the vulnerable path. `mip_rx` aliases the attacker-controlled buffer pointer and byte count into packet state that later drives the IPv4, ICMP, and payload-length logic.
source.value_from: The staged witness is the exact 131071-byte file `gt_results/arvo_51757/poc` with SHA-256 `e8501c7cc11c4a09faee601b0eab9bbeaf150d98ea5aeced79e6e304128c49bd`. Bytes 0..5 are destination MAC `00:00:00:00:00:00`, bytes 12..13 are Ethernet type `08 00`, byte 23 is IP protocol `01`, bytes 30..33 are destination IP `00 00 00 00`, byte 34 is ICMP type `08`, and the remaining bytes from offset 38 onward are the payload copied at the sink.
source.note: The fuzz target call `mip_rx(ifp, (void *) data, size)` in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` is the unscored harness boundary; this assignment pair is the first project statement that materializes `data,size` into vulnerability-relevant state.

sink.description: Unchecked write sink. `rx_icmp` copies the full attacker-controlled payload into the fixed transmit-buffer payload region starting at `icmp + 1`.
sink.note: In the staged line map this `memcpy` is line 453; the saved ASan trace reports the same callsite as `rx_icmp ... mip/mip.c:454:5`, then faults in `__asan_memcpy` with `WRITE of size 131033`.

root_cause.description: The only guard in the vulnerable ICMP receive path checks echo-request type and destination IP; it does not require that the derived payload length fit the fixed transmit buffer.
root_cause.note: The witness satisfies `type == 8` and `pkt->ip->dst == ifp->ip == 0`, so control enters the copy path. The missing obligation is the later `left` clamp introduced by metadata commit `a88a11c2` and finalized in `9680b8cc`.

parser_admitted.description: After the destination-MAC filter accepts the frame, `mip_rx` selects the IPv4 parser arm for the witness Ethernet type `0x0800`.
parser_admitted.note: The preceding MAC check also passes because `cfg = {}` leaves `ifp->mac` all zero and the witness destination MAC is likewise `00:00:00:00:00:00`; the subsequent version check accepts IP version 4 from header byte `0x49`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement materializes the attacker-controlled ICMP payload span as the remaining bytes from pointer `p` to the end of the raw buffer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the crashing call from `rx_ip`, `p = pkt->icmp + 1`, i.e. raw input offset 38. With `pkt.raw.len = 131071`, this computes `pkt->pay.len = 131033` and `pkt->pay.buf = buf + 38`.
tainted_value_origin.note: Because the ICMP path never consults the IPv4 IHL or total-length fields, the oversized trailing portion of the witness survives intact as `pkt->pay`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness fixes `pktlen = 1540`, allocates stack object `t` to hold `mip_if` plus RX/TX packet buffers, initializes `ifp`, and forwards the exact 131071-byte witness into `mip_rx`.
`if_init` maps `ifp->tx` to a fixed 1540-byte transmit buffer inside that stack object.
The raw bytes are aliased into `pkt`, accepted as an IPv4 frame for the zeroed interface MAC, and forwarded to `rx_ip`.
The IPv4 ICMP path materializes `pkt->icmp` and computes `pkt->pay` as the full remaining input after fixed Ethernet/IP/ICMP headers, yielding `pkt->pay.len = 131033`.
The echo-request/destination guard passes, but no transmit-buffer size guard exists, so `memcpy` writes the 131033-byte payload into only 1502 bytes of TX payload space and triggers AddressSanitizer.

fine_trace.code:
size_t pktlen = 1540;
char t[sizeof(struct mip_if) + pktlen * 2 + 0 /* qlen */];
fine_trace.note: Harness step. The fuzz target fixes `pktlen = 1540` and allocates a VLA-backed stack object `t` that stores the `mip_if` plus one 1540-byte RX buffer and one 1540-byte TX buffer. The later overflow lands inside this stack object, which is why ASan classifies the fault as dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.code:
ifp->rx.buf = (uint8_t *) (ifp + 1), ifp->rx.len = maxpktsize;
ifp->tx.buf = ifp->rx.buf + maxpktsize, ifp->tx.len = maxpktsize;
fine_trace.note: Project setup step. The call from the harness passes `maxpktsize = pktlen = 1540`, so `if_init` makes `ifp->tx` the second 1540-byte slice inside `t`. Every later ICMP response write must stay within this fixed-size region.
Source step. `mip_rx` aliases the exact witness buffer and size into `pkt.raw`, preserving the full 131071-byte span for later header parsing and payload-length derivation.

After the destination-MAC filter accepts the frame, the IPv4 arm is taken because the witness Ethernet type is `0x0800` and the version nibble is 4. `pkt.ip` now points at the raw IPv4 header whose destination is `0.0.0.0` and protocol is ICMP (`1`).

`rx_ip` takes the ICMP branch because `pkt->ip->proto == 1` and materializes the ICMP header immediately after the fixed 20-byte `struct ip`. On the witness, `pkt->icmp->type` is `8`, so the request is an echo packet.

Called from `rx_ip` with `p = pkt->icmp + 1`, this computes the payload as every remaining byte after the fixed Ethernet/IP/ICMP headers. For the 131071-byte witness, `pkt->pay.buf` becomes `buf + 38` and `pkt->pay.len` becomes `131033`. The ICMP path does not clamp this by the IPv4 IHL byte `0x49` or the total-length field `0x0003`.

Root-cause step. The only guard for the response path checks echo-request type and interface IP. Because `cfg = {}` left `ifp->ip == 0` and the witness destination IP is `0.0.0.0`, control enters the block. There is no guard or clamp that requires `pkt->pay.len` to fit the fixed `ifp->tx` buffer before the copy.

`tx_ip` lays the Ethernet and IPv4 headers at the start of `ifp->tx.buf`, so `icmp + 1` points 38 bytes into the 1540-byte TX buffer. That leaves only `1540 - 38 = 1502` payload bytes available at the destination of the upcoming copy.

Sink step. The copy length stays attacker-controlled at `131033`, but the destination region from step 8 holds only 1502 payload bytes. This `memcpy` therefore writes far past the end of the VLA-backed stack object `t`, reproducing the saved `AddressSanitizer: dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 131033` in `rx_icmp`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan stack reports `rx_icmp` at line 454 because the instrumented build resolves the fault through `__asan_memcpy`; the reproduced staged checkout's exact line map places the crashing `memcpy(icmp + 1, pkt->pay.buf, pkt->pay.len)` call at line 453 in the same function.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not applicable: this is a dynamic stack-buffer-overflow into the harness VLA `t`, so there is no separate heap allocation/free context to match.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved project stack is `rx_icmp -> rx_ip -> mip_rx -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, and the fine trace refines that same path with the earlier `if_init` buffer-extent setup and `mkpay` payload-length derivation that have already executed before frame 0 faults.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_51757 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/fuzz` and produced `AddressSanitizer: dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 131033` in `rx_icmp` with stack `rx_icmp -> rx_ip -> mip_rx`.

format.name: Mongoose MIP raw IPv4 ICMP echo frame
format.contract: Exactly the staged 131071-byte file `gt_results/arvo_51757/poc` with SHA-256 `e8501c7cc11c4a09faee601b0eab9bbeaf150d98ea5aeced79e6e304128c49bd`. Its destination MAC is `00:00:00:00:00:00`, Ethernet type is `0x0800`, the fixed IPv4 header bytes used by this path encode version nibble `4`, protocol `1`, and destination IP `0.0.0.0`, and byte 34 is ICMP type `8`. On the reproduced path, `mip_rx`/`rx_ip` ignore the witness IPv4 IHL (`0x49`) and total-length (`0x0003`) fields for ICMP payload sizing, so every byte from offset 38 to EOF becomes `pkt->pay`, i.e. 131033 bytes. The harness fixes `pktlen = 1540`, so `if_init` makes only 1540 bytes of TX space available and `rx_icmp` has only 1502 payload bytes after headers. Vulnerable `rx_icmp` then copies all 131033 payload bytes into that 1502-byte region, reproducing the saved overflow. The staged evidence proves only this exact witness layout and observed path; it does not justify a broader claim about arbitrary oversized ICMP packets.
